newsitem.title: GREECE: SIX BANKS TO BID FOR BANK/CENTRAL GREECE - AGROBANK.
newsitem.headline: SIX BANKS TO BID FOR BANK/CENTRAL GREECE - AGROBANK.

text.p: Six Greek and foreign banks
confirmed their interest in bidding for Bank of Central Greece
and received the information memorandum and due
diligence report, said state Agricultural Bank of Greece.
The six credit institutions are the following:
Bank of Nova Scotia
Egnatia Bank
Hellenic Bank of Cyprus
Euromerchant
Aspis Group
Piraeus Bank
Agricultural Bank owns about 56 percent of common registered
shares and 21 percent of preferred registered shares of the Bank
of Central Greece.
Bank of Central Greece was founded in 1936 and was listed on
the Athens bourse in 1991. It has a network of 22 branches and
employs 580.
The deadline for the submission of bids for a majority stake
in Bank of Central Greece is set for June 25, it said.
"The privatisation of the Bank of Central Greece proceeds
according to time plans and June 25 is the deadline for the
submission of binding bids for a majority stake in it," it said.
Agricultural Bank and the government were optimistic about
the privatisation process.
"There is optimism regarding the privatisation of the Bank
of Central Greece on the side of Agricultural Bank's management
as well as on the government, which closely monitors the sale
process," it said.
Agricultural Bank retained ABN AMRO Bank and Deloitte &
Touche as advisors on the sale earlier this year.
In May 23, Ergobank , Greece's second largest
private bank, withdrew its bid for a majority stake in the Bank
of Central Greece.
ErgoBank cited an extra condition in the tender which asked
bidders to refrain from reassigning staff positions at the Bank
of Central Greece.
This, it said, justified its decision to withdraw its bid
because no distinction was drawn between total employment levels
and current job descriptions.
--Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
